fix_assessment.rationale: No existing fix attempt covers Offline Files results in the Windows Search plugin.

issue_context.summary: PowerToys Run's Windows Search plugin omits files from a synced Offline Files network share even though Windows Start search finds the indexed local cache entries.
known_information: The report gives deterministic setup and comparison steps.
Windows Start search finds the files after the share is marked Always available offline.
The PowerToys Run plugin queries the SystemIndex catalog independently from Start.
inferences: The plugin's hardcoded scope='file:' restriction or ItemUrl-to-LocalPath conversion may exclude Offline Files/CSC index entries that Start includes.
issue_context.analysis: Current WindowsSearchAPI uses SystemIndex but adds a fixed file scope and converts System.ItemUrl through Uri.LocalPath. A focused local reproduction can inspect the raw indexed URL and generated SQL to determine whether filtering or conversion drops the result.
initial_investigation: The result path is derived from System.ItemUrl through Uri.LocalPath.
No pull request referencing issue 12503 was found.

actions.label: P

proposed_fixes.title: Include indexed Offline Files entries in PowerToys Run
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The plugin likely filters out CSC/offline-share entries with its fixed file scope or fails to normalize their System.ItemUrl into a usable UNC/local cache path.
plan: Capture the generated SQL and raw System.ItemUrl for a file that Start finds in an offline share.
Adjust scope/URL normalization only for indexed file records, preserving hidden-file and excluded-pattern filters.
Add an abstraction-level test for file, UNC, and Offline Files item URLs plus an integration fixture when CSC is available.
verification: Search the same offline file from Start and PowerToys Run and verify matching results open the intended network/offline path.

confidence.rationale: The query restriction is a plausible concrete discriminator, but a CSC SystemIndex row is needed to select scope filtering versus URI conversion.
